While not explicitly labeled as short-seller targets, MRK’s fundamentals align with classic bear and activist critique criteria: valuation resilience versus fundamental erosion, capital allocation discipline, and binary execution risk. Merck faces escalating regulatory scrutiny and multi-layered litigation risk. On the pricing front, a December 2025 agreement with the U.S. government committed the company to over $70 billion in domestic investment while expanding direct-to-patient access for diabetes drugs at materially lower prices, signaling intense political and payer pressure to control pharmaceutical costs [4]. This aligns with broader industry trends where governments and insurers aggressively restrict pricing power, compounding margin risks [6]. Legally, Merck remains exposed to significant product liability litigation. In February 2026, a U.S. district court partially granted and denied a motion to dismiss in the Kaiser case regarding Gardasil, adjourning the trial to May 4, 2026; Merck continues to vigorously defend against claims linking the vaccine to plaintiff injuries [7].
